preamble: This is the late Bunthorne's last puzzle.

clue.text: Slid on heel, can't repair the weak spot

indicators.note: to repair is to put back together, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone slipped on a heel and cannot mend the weak part of the shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair' signals the anagram of SLIDONHEELCANT. The surface suggests a broken shoe heel, but the heel of the foot is where the answer lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles was vulnerable only at his heel, so the phrase is an idiom for any fatal vulnerability.

clue.text: Mad dog for one transferred from the Marx oeuvre

indicators.note: the two pieces are swapped round from the order the clue reads them

parts.note: a dog is one example of an animal
crackers is informal British for mad

explanation.surface: A rabid dog has been shifted out of the Marx Brothers' body of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transferred' tells you the clue's order, mad then dog, is switched: the dog piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 1930 Marx Brothers film, one work in their output.

clue.text: Elsewhere synods embracing auto-da-fé for this

indicators.note: the words hold the run of letters within them, as if hugging it

explanation.surface: Church councils in other places punished something by burning at the stake.
explanation.walkthrough: An auto-da-fé was the Inquisition's public sentencing, often to burning, so the definition describes the crime it punished.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inquisition's autos-da-fé were the punishment for religious unorthodoxy, the offence named here.

clue.text: Not netting around big fish

indicators.note: the fish's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: the ling is a long sea fish
OS is the abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Failing to land anything in the net while surrounded by large fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big fish' reads as one phrase but splits between two pieces. 'Not netting' means failing to make a net profit, not failing to catch fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A business not netting anything is running at a loss, failing to make a profit.

clue.text: Mother's raw material for chicken feed

indicators.note: raw material is stuff to be worked up, so these letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A mother's unprocessed supplies are destined to feed the poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken feed' usually means a trivial sum of money; here it is literal food that hens scratch up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hens peck worms out of the soil, so the creatures literally serve as poultry food.

clue.text: See 1 across
Fruit with an evening in Paris: eat English and throw up!

indicators.note: in a down entry, throwing up sends the whole run upwards, so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: An evening out in Paris: eating English food and being sick afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throw up' in a down clue reverses SOIREATE, the three pieces together, upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An etaerio is a botanist's term for an aggregate fruit such as a raspberry or strawberry.

clue.text: Did Bunthorne shy stone at first travelling folk?

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, so I

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Did the setter hurl a rock first at the wandering people?
explanation.walkthrough: 'shy' looks like a verb meaning throw, but it is the adjective, COY. The setter's pseudonym stands for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Didicoy is a British term for an itinerant, a traveller or gypsy.

clue.text: Upstarts? Excuse our havin' blundered

indicators.note: something blundered has gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Social climbers make excuses for having made a hash of things.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase names people newly rich but lacking social polish, i.e. upstarts.

clue.text: Ireland is cleaving Bremner for mocking

indicators.note: the word splits the other open by going into it

parts.note: Rory Bremner is a British comedian and impressionist

explanation.surface: Ireland is splitting the impressionist Bremner, who mimics people.
explanation.walkthrough: Rory Bremner is a well-known British satirical impressionist, which suits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Irrisory is a rare word for derisive, given to laughing at or ridiculing.

clue.text: Theologian has turned to embrace holy man, refined

indicators.note: the reversed word wraps round the other piece
the preceding word is turned round to read backwards

explanation.surface: A theologian has turned towards hugging a cultured holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses HAS to SAH, which then embraces DD.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu (also spelt saddhu) is a Hindu holy man or ascetic.

clue.text: Cracked basin the Degas drinkers put down

indicators.note: a cracked basin is broken, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Drinkers set a broken washbasin down, as in a Degas painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Degas painted L'Absinthe, showing two drinkers in a café; 'put down' means put on canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Degas's painting shows a woman with a glass of the green spirit, the drink he portrayed.

clue.text: Councillor to augment outdated nursery provision

parts.note: eche is an archaic verb meaning to increase

explanation.surface: A local councillor wants to expand old-fashioned childcare.
explanation.definitionFit: A crèche is a day nursery where young children are looked after.

clue.text: Mature tirade about oriental contaminant

indicators.note: the tirade is on the subject of, and placed after, the oriental piece

parts.note: a rant is a long angry speech

explanation.surface: A grown-up delivers an angry speech about something from the East that is polluting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as concerning: a RANT about E, which follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulterant is a substance added to make something impure, a contaminant.

clue.text: Well done, the solver! That was Erin's stout assertion!

definitions.meaning: a cheer of congratulation to the person finishing
Guinness, the Irish stout, long advertised itself with this slogan; Erin is Ireland

explanation.surface: Congratulating the solver while recalling an Irish beer advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an expression of praise, and the famous Guinness advertising slogan about health.

clue.text: See 1 down
By what authority? I'm umpire! Out!

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An umpire answers a challenge to his authority by giving a batter out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out!' reads as the umpire's decision, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperium is Latin for command or supreme authority, the power the umpire claims.

clue.text: How a marathon competitor comes across and collides?

definitions.text: How a marathon competitor comes across
definitions.meaning: a racer arrives at the finish line on foot, and to come across is to meet by chance

explanation.surface: A marathon runner meets someone and bumps into them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to meet by chance and to crash against something.

clue.text: Odd! The Guardian's economist here with unconfirmed reports

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd
the newspaper speaks of itself as ours
John Stuart Mill, the political economist

explanation.surface: Strange: the newspaper's economist is here passing on gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumour mill is the source or place from which unverified gossip spreads.

clue.text: Petty officer can raise a child

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising the word lifts it upwards, reading it backwards

explanation.surface: A minor officer is able to bring up a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb, but it is the noun TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tindal was a petty officer among lascar sailors in India.

clue.text: Marianne personified as fantastic broad: a model!

indicators.note: fantastic suggests wild change, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the Model T Ford gives T

explanation.surface: France's emblem embodied as an amazing woman: a model.
explanation.walkthrough: Marianne is the symbol of France, and Brigitte Bardot was the model for her bust in 1969.
explanation.definitionFit: The actress Brigitte Bardot was chosen as the face of France's national emblem.

clue.text: See 8
As insincere as a smile from Cheshire?

definitions.text: As insincere as a smile from Cheshire?

parts.words: As insincere as a smile from Cheshire?
parts.note: Cheshire is a famous English cheese, and a grin from it would be overdone and false, as is the Cheshire Cat's grin

explanation.surface: A false grin like that of the Cheshire Cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheesy grin is a broad but insincere smile, and Cheshire is also a cheese.

clue.text: A tricky problem: with ie not one calorie in Madame Butterfly's cuisine

indicators.note: a problem is a puzzle to work out, so the letters are reordered
IE takes the place of the calorie letter

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for calorie

explanation.surface: A dieting puzzle: cutting a calorie from Japanese food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one' swaps C (calorie) for IE in A TRICKY, giving ATRIKYIE, which 'problem' rearranges. Madame Butterfly is Japanese.
explanation.definitionFit: Teriyaki is a Japanese method of glazing grilled food, and the opera's heroine is Japanese.

clue.text: Lamb devotees beginning to eat escargot over here!

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used
the word is turned over, reading backwards

explanation.surface: Fans of lamb start eating snails in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: Lamb is Charles Lamb, the essayist who wrote as Elia; 'over' reverses SNAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Elians are admirers of Charles Lamb, who wrote his essays under the name Elia.

clue.text: Had I had trouble with Liberal revolutionary, would be affected

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so the letters are mixed
revolution turns things over, a second signal that the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Had I got into difficulties with a radical Liberal, I would have been moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' reads as emotionally moved, but it means pretentious.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da describes pretentious or affected manners and speech.

clue.text: Ascetic wobbling 'til on 'is stem? Yes!

indicators.note: something wobbling is unsteady, so the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A holy man teeters on his pillar, asking himself whether to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: The saint lived for decades on top of a pillar, so wobbling there is part of the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: This Syrian saint was an ascetic who lived on top of a column for 37 years.

clue.text: See 26
